ca_split_rock_2.blurb: Split Rock is a small formation high in the Sugarloaf area on the Highway 50 corridor, between Placerville and Tahoe, at roughly 4,600 feet. The crag takes its name from a large split running through the stone. There are nine routes, eight of them bolted sport lines and one trad. Grades run from 5.6 up to the 5.10 range: two at 5.6, two at 5.9 and five in the 5.10s. The bolts are placed close together and the way on and off the top is simple, which makes it a handy stop for warming up or for practising leading on single-pitch lines. It sits right beside the main trail close to the Sugarloaf itself.

ca_solarium_boulder.blurb: Solarium Boulder is a large block in the Central Happiness part of the Happy Boulders, in the Volcanic Tablelands outside Bishop, at about 4,500 feet. Its west face leans back slightly and is dotted with pockets. Nine problems share the boulder, spanning V1 to V10: a handful in the V1 to V4 range, then a few much harder lines at V7, V9 and V10. The wider area is known for pocketed, steep and gymnastic climbing on closely spaced boulders with flat landings. The boulder stands beside the main trail through the canyon, near the Happy Boulder itself.

ca_savannah_boulder.blurb: Savannah Boulder is a big, obvious block on the right of the trail in the Savannah area of the Happy Boulders, a short way up the canyon past Girlfriend Boulder, near Bishop in the Volcanic Tablelands. It holds nine problems and the grades stay low: from VB through V4, with most of them between V2 and V4. A few of the harder ones ask for sound technique as well as strength. Because the grades are modest, it suits climbers working up from the V0 and V2 range as well as those ticking off the V4s. Nearby boulders in the same canyon give plenty to link into a session.

ca_super_dome_the.blurb: The Super Dome is a prominent formation on the north Wonderland skyline in Joshua Tree National Park, next to Willow Hole at about 4,300 feet. It carries nine routes, eight trad and one sport, from 5.7 up to 5.12. Most sit in the 5.10 range, with a couple of 5.11 and 5.12 lines on top. The routes tend toward hard climbing, thin protection, or both, and several run to multiple pitches. Reaching the base takes a long hike and some slab scrambling, so this is a committed day in a wilderness setting rather than a quick roadside stop.

ca_wood_cutters_wall.blurb: Wood Cutters Wall sits in Crystal Springs Canyon, part of Woodfords Canyon along Highway 88 near Carson Pass, at about 6,500 feet. Getting there takes an extra uphill walk beyond the neighbouring Strangler Cliff. There are nine routes, mostly trad with a single sport line, and the grades run from 5.7 to 5.12: two at 5.7, one 5.8, two 5.9, two in the 5.10s, then a 5.11 and a 5.12. The canyon as a whole is known for crack climbing, and the lines here fit that pattern. A handful of obvious features dominate the wall, and a short scramble is needed to reach the ridge.

ca_lower_tier_4.blurb: The Lower Tier is the bottom of three tiers on Stonewall Peak in San Diego County, and it is the rightmost one as seen from the approach trail. All nine routes are trad, running from 5.7 to 5.9: one at 5.7, three at 5.8 and five at 5.9. The stone is crumbly in places and can be unforgiving on face moves, and its grainy texture causes heavy rope drag, so longer slings and back-cleaning gear help. The routes are traditional lines rather than polished sport climbs.
